title: Example Lab releases Nova-2, a faster mid-size language model
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. Example Lab introduced Nova-2, a mid-size model it says matches last year's flagship on coding benchmarks at a third of the cost. The model is available today through the lab's API and in its chat app, with a 1M-token context window and new controls for how long it reasons before answering.

title: AI chip startup raises $900 million to build inference data centers
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. A two-year-old chip designer closed a $900 million round to build data centers specialized for running, rather than training, AI models. Investors cited falling prices for model access as a sign that demand is shifting toward cheap, high-volume inference.

title: EU publishes first enforcement guidance for general-purpose AI models
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. The European Commission published guidance explaining how it will check compliance for providers of general-purpose AI models. The document covers documentation duties, copyright summaries and incident reporting, and gives companies six months to adapt.

title: Open-source toolkit makes fine-tuning small models possible on a laptop
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. A new open-source library lets developers fine-tune models of up to 8 billion parameters on a consumer laptop using memory-saving techniques. The release includes ready-made recipes for chat, classification and summarization.

title: Study finds AI coding assistants cut review time but raise bug rates
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. Researchers tracked 400 developers for six months and found pull requests written with AI assistance were reviewed 30 percent faster. However, they also contained slightly more bugs that reached production, suggesting teams need stronger automated testing.

title: Example Lab adds scheduled tasks to its developer platform
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. Developers can now run agent jobs on a schedule without hosting their own servers. The feature supports cron syntax and sends results to a webhook.

title: Chain-of-verification reduces hallucinations in long-form answers
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. We propose a method in which a model drafts an answer, plans verification questions, answers them independently and revises the draft. On four benchmarks the approach reduces factual errors by up to 28 percent.

title: A benchmark for agents that operate spreadsheets
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. We introduce a benchmark of 1,200 real-world spreadsheet tasks such as cleaning data and building pivot tables. The best current agents complete 61 percent of tasks, compared with 92 percent for human experts.

title: Phone maker ships on-device assistant that works offline
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. A major phone maker began rolling out an assistant that runs entirely on the device, so it keeps working without a connection. The company says no voice data leaves the phone.

title: Cloud provider signs multi-year deal to host a lab's models
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. A large cloud provider agreed to supply computing capacity to an AI lab over five years. Terms were not disclosed, but analysts estimate the deal at several billion dollars.

title: US state passes law requiring labels on AI-generated political ads
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. Lawmakers approved a bill requiring clear labels on political advertising that uses AI-generated images, audio or video. The law takes effect before next year's elections.

title: New open-weight speech model transcribes 90 languages
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. An open-weight speech recognition model covering 90 languages was released under a permissive license. It runs in real time on a single consumer GPU.

title: Robots learn household chores from a few minutes of video
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. A university team showed robots learning tasks like folding towels after watching short videos of people. The approach needs far less demonstration data than earlier methods.

title: Startup building AI tutors for schools reaches one million students
excerpt: SAMPLE ARTICLE. An education startup said its AI tutoring app is now used by one million students across 20 countries. Teachers can see each student's progress and set limits on what the tutor answers.
